question: Which syringe and needle setup is best for giving a Mantoux skin test?

options.A: A 1-mL tuberculin syringe with a short 27-gauge fine needle
options.B: A 5-mL syringe with a blunt-tip drawing needle
options.C: An insulin syringe marked in units with a permanent attached needle
options.D: A 3-mL syringe with a large 21-gauge intramuscular needle

explanation: You need a tiny syringe to measure tiny drops accurately, and a short, fine needle helps you slide the fluid right into the top layers of the skin! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h3)

question: Why do high-risk strains of HPV require regular cervical screening even when a woman feels fine?

options.A: High-risk HPV can cause silent cellular changes in the cervix that lead to cancer over time
options.B: Routine screening is the only way to clear the virus completely from nerve tissues
options.C: HPV bacteria become resistant to standard antibiotic therapies if left unchecked
options.D: The virus rapidly destroys red blood cells and causes severe systemic anemia

explanation: High-risk HPV can change cervical cells without causing any pain or warning signs. That's why routine Pap smears are so lifesaving! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T2#GNS216_U5_T2_h4)

question: Which microscopic blood vessels act as the primary control valves for blood entering capillary beds?

options.A: Capillaries
options.B: Vena cava
options.C: Arterioles
options.D: Venules

explanation: Arterioles have smooth muscle walls that constrict or dilate to control the volume of blood flowing into local capillary networks. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why is the formulary tied closely to the National Essential Medicines List?

options.A: It replaces the need for nurses to study pharmacology in school
options.B: It ensures hospitals stock medicines needed for the most common illnesses
options.C: It forces pharmaceutical companies to stop importing foreign products
options.D: It guarantees that every citizen receives free treatment at clinics

explanation: Spot on! Linking them makes sure hospitals focus on stocking the drugs our patients need most, like treatments for malaria and common infections. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T5#GNS215_U1_T5_h1)

question: When we talk about pharmacodynamics, what are we mainly looking at?

options.A: How the kidneys excrete drug metabolites
options.B: The rate of drug absorption in the gut
options.C: What drugs do to the body
options.D: How the liver breaks down drugs

explanation: Think of pharmacodynamics simply as what the drug does *to* the body (like lowering your blood pressure or easing pain). You've got this! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T6#GNS125_U1_T6_h1)

question: What is the proper way to hold clean linen when you are about to make a bed?

options.A: Tuck the clean linen under your arm to keep both hands free
options.B: Rest the clean linen pile on the patient's bedside table for easy access
options.C: Place the clean linen on the floor temporarily while gathering equipment
options.D: Hold the clean linen away from your uniform to prevent contamination

explanation: Well done! Your uniform picks up germs from different places, so keeping clean sheets away from your body keeps them germ-free for the patient. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h2)

question: A client is charting her basal body temperature (BBT). What is the key thing she must know about this method?

options.A: It prevents pregnancy by killing sperm in the uterus.
options.B: It measures hormone levels inside her bloodstream directly.
options.C: It confirms that ovulation has already taken place.
options.D: It predicts the exact hour ovulation will happen today.

explanation: Because the slight temperature jump is driven by progesterone *after* release, BBT charting is great for confirming ovulation happened, rather than predicting it ahead of time. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T7#GNS121_U5_T7_h6)

question: Which part of the early blastocyst grows to become the baby's side of the placenta?

options.A: Amniotic cavity
options.B: Zona pellucida
options.C: Trophoblast
options.D: Inner cell mass

explanation: You've got this! The outer layer, called the trophoblast, reaches out to connect with the mother's uterine lining to form the placenta. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T4#GNS121_U6_T4_h1)

question: What makes communication in home health care different from a hospital setting?

options.A: Communication is restricted by hospital rules
options.B: Nurses rely solely on written medical charts
options.C: The nurse enters a private home as a guest
options.D: Patients have no family members present

explanation: Stepping into a patient's personal space completely changes the dynamic! Unlike a controlled clinic, you are a guest in their domain, which calls for extra respect and adaptability. [learn more](GNS324_U2_T3#GNS324_U2_T3_h1)

question: Why do people lose weight so fast in the first few days of a strict fad diet?

options.A: Instantaneous healing of the gastrointestinal lining
options.B: Permanent destruction of abnormal fat cells in the abdomen
options.C: Loss of body water and breakdown of stored muscle protein
options.D: Rapid increase in physical activity levels induced by supplements

explanation: That quick drop on the scale isn't fat—it's mostly water weight and muscle glycogen being used up. Good to know as a future nurse! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T018#GNS227_U2_T018_h4)

question: Why is proper documentation of contraceptive counseling important in the client's health record?

options.A: It stops the client from ever changing her birth control method later
options.B: It proves to the hospital management that the nurse worked full hours
options.C: It guarantees that the healthcare facility will receive extra government funding
options.D: It ensures continuity of care and creates a legal record of the client's informed choices

explanation: Clear records allow other healthcare providers to know what method was chosen, what education was given, and what follow-up is needed. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T015#GNS226_U5_T015_h7)

question: What happens when you empower nurses in a clinical unit?

options.A: Reduced need for continuing education programs
options.B: Increased professional autonomy and job satisfaction
options.C: Complete elimination of shift handovers
options.D: Shorter educational requirements for new graduates

explanation: Empowerment gives nurses the confidence to make sound clinical decisions, which makes them happier and more fulfilled in their jobs! [learn more](GST321_U1_T14#GST321_U1_T14_h5)

question: Which part of the teenage brain develops much slower than the emotional center?

options.A: The prefrontal cortex
options.B: The cerebellum
options.C: The brainstem
options.D: The occipital lobe

explanation: The prefrontal cortex (the brain's planning and logic center) takes its time maturing, which explains why teens sometimes act on strong emotions before thinking things through! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T4#GNS312_U3_T4_h3)

question: When is the best time for a first follow-up visit after putting in an IUD (Intrauterine Device)?

options.A: After six months
options.B: After exactly five years
options.C: After twenty-four hours
options.D: After four to six weeks

explanation: Seeing the client at 4 to 6 weeks lets you check the IUD strings and make sure the device hasn't slipped out. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T024#GNS226_U6_T024_h2)

question: A patient's lab report comes back with a critical panic value. What is your immediate nursing action?

options.A: Document the laboratory value in the chart and resume other tasks
options.B: Wait until the end of the shift to report the result during handoff
options.C: Notify the provider urgently and assess the patient at the bedside
options.D: Repeat the exact same blood draw yourself to confirm the mistake

explanation: A critical panic value means danger! Your first steps are to check on your patient right away at the bedside and notify the doctor immediately. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h8)

question: You see a toddler running around the living room while eating crackers. What should you do first?

options.A: Wait until the child finishes running to intervene.
options.B: Take the food away immediately and scold the child.
options.C: Calmly ask the child to sit at the table before eating more.
options.D: Offer the child a cup of water to wash down the crackers.

explanation: Great nursing judgment! Running and eating is a major recipe for choking. Gently guiding them to sit down keeps them safe with a smile. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T7#GNS324_U6_T7_h4)

question: What do we study in microbiology?

options.A: The structural anatomy of multicellular forest plants
options.B: The breeding and management of large domesticated livestock
options.C: Organisms too small to see without a microscope
options.D: The chemical composition of rocks and mineral deposits

explanation: Microbiology is simply the study of tiny life forms like bacteria and viruses that need lenses to be seen clearly. You've got this! [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h1)

question: What two main things interact during a serological test to confirm a microbe is present?

options.A: Peptidoglycan and crystal violet
options.B: Agar and nutrient broth
options.C: Hydrogen peroxide and catalase
options.D: Antigens and antibodies

explanation: You got it! Serology relies on the precise lock-and-key fit between the germ's antigens and our body's antibodies. [learn more](GST114_U5_T3#GST114_U5_T3_h6)

question: What is a key nursing duty right before an upper GI (throat and esophagus) dilation?

options.A: Administering a heavy oral laxative to clear the esophagus
options.B: Ensuring removable dental appliances are taken out
options.C: Instructing the patient to drink large volumes of water
options.D: Placing a heavy weighted blanket over the patient's chest

explanation: False teeth or removable dental plates can easily pop loose and block the airway during throat procedures, so they must always be taken out first. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T19#GNS212_U1_T19_h4)

question: What is a major cause of strain on traditional family elder care systems in Nigeria?

options.A: Mandatory government placement of all seniors into nursing homes
options.B: A complete cultural loss of respect for older family members
options.C: Urbanization and the migration of younger relatives to cities
options.D: The total absence of any chronic health conditions in the elderly

explanation: As younger family members move to urban centers for work, the traditional extended family network available at home to care for elders is stretched thin. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T8#GNS225_U5_T8_h7)

question: Which of these is a key behavioral warning sign that a school-aged child might be at risk?

options.A: Sudden and unexplained drop in academic performance
options.B: Consistent completion of all assigned homework tasks
options.C: Increased enthusiasm for structured extracurricular sports
options.D: Active participation in school health club meetings

explanation: Well done! A sudden, unexplained crash in grades usually means a child is dealing with hidden stress, abuse, or negative peer pressure. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T4#GNS225_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is required before giving any medication authorized by a standing order?

options.A: Asking the patient to pay double the standard consultation fee
options.B: Waiting for a written countersignature from the state governor
options.C: Storing the medication in direct sunlight for at least one hour
options.D: Verifying the safety rights such as right patient, drug, and dose

explanation: Standard drug administration safety rules must always be followed, regardless of whether a drug is given via a standing order or a direct prescription. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT typically evaluated during a standard newborn Apgar check?

options.A: Blood glucose level
options.B: Muscle tone
options.C: Skin color
options.D: Heart rate

explanation: The Apgar score assesses appearance, pulse, grimace, activity, and respiration; blood glucose is a lab test, not an Apgar parameter. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h6)

question: According to the healthy plate model, how much of your meal should be fruits and non-starchy veggies?

options.A: The entire plate
options.B: One-half
options.C: One-quarter
options.D: Three-quarters

explanation: Half the plate! Packing it with veggies and fruits gives you great fiber and vitamins without overloading on calories. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T003#GNS227_U2_T003_h5)

question: A patient with long-term severe bronchitis has a higher risk for which type of urine leakage?

options.A: Overflow incontinence due to a blocked prostate
options.B: Stress incontinence due to repeated pressure from coughing
options.C: Urge incontinence due to bladder muscle irritation
options.D: Functional incontinence due to immobility

explanation: Constant coughing creates repeated downward pressure on the pelvic floor, which can wear down its support over time. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T18#GNS212_U1_T18_h4)

question: What happens when a nurse washes their hands properly between patients?

options.A: It permanently cures the patient of chronic illnesses
options.B: It creates a new portal of entry for beneficial flora
options.C: It breaks the mode of transmission link in the chain
options.D: It destroys the genetic material of the reservoir host

explanation: Handwashing removes or kills germs, stopping them from traveling from one person to another. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T81#GNS214_U1_T81_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to holistic nursing practice in busy hospitals?

options.A: Hierarchical medical structures that limit nursing autonomy
options.B: Abundant staffing levels with too many nurses on every shift
options.C: Task-oriented routines focused only on quick medication rounds
options.D: Heavy workloads and high patient-to-nurse ratios

explanation: Great catch! Staff shortages and heavy workloads are major barriers in our hospitals, so abundant staffing is definitely not one of them. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is keeping a food diary helpful for someone with gas issues?

options.A: It completely cures lactose intolerance without any medication.
options.B: It measures the exact volume of gas produced each hour.
options.C: It helps the patient and nurse pinpoint specific foods that trigger excess gas.
options.D: It guarantees the patient will lose weight within the first week.

explanation: Writing down meals and symptoms helps connect the dots so patients can figure out which foods don't agree with them. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T10#GNS212_U1_T10_h7)

question: Why should a community health nurse view the entire community as their 'client'?

options.A: It prevents nurses from having to examine individual patients
options.B: Individual health is deeply connected to broader community functions
options.C: Hospital administrators require nurses to count every resident
options.D: Local laws prohibit nurses from treating people one at a time

explanation: Brilliant! Looking at the whole community helps you tackle root issues like poverty, environment, and culture that affect every single patient. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T4#GNS225_U1_T4_h7)

question: Which of these actions breaks basic infection control rules during elimination care?

options.A: Wearing clean gloves while emptying a urine collection container
options.B: Placing a used bedpan on the patient's overbed table
options.C: Keeping the call bell within reach of the patient
options.D: Washing hands before and after providing perineal care

explanation: Yikes! Overbed tables are meant for clean things like food and drinks. Putting a dirty bedpan there spreads germs where people eat. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T8#GNS112_U5_T8_h6)

question: Why do intramuscular injections get absorbed faster than subcutaneous ones?

options.A: Subcutaneous fat contains no blood vessels
options.B: Muscles produce enzymes that break down drugs
options.C: The needle used is always much thinner
options.D: Muscle tissue has a rich blood supply

explanation: Great job thinking about how drugs move in the body! Muscles have plenty of blood vessels, which helps medications rush quickly into the bloodstream. You've got this! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T3#GNS122_U1_T3_h1)

question: A patient with thick lung secretions refuses to drink water because of nausea. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Force the patient to drink a full cup of water immediately
options.B: Report the fluid refusal and suggest IV hydration or anti-nausea medication
options.C: Document that the patient refuses care and leave the room
options.D: Stop all respiratory treatments until the nausea goes away on its own

explanation: Good hydration thins out thick mucus so it can be cleared easily. Addressing nausea and providing fluids through alternative routes helps maintain airway clearance. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h2)

question: When is a scheduled caesarean section typically recommended for a pregnant woman living with HIV?

options.A: When the baby is presenting in a normal vertex position
options.B: When her viral load is high or unknown near delivery
options.C: When the mother prefers surgical delivery for convenience
options.D: When she has been taking her ART medications strictly

explanation: A planned caesarean delivery before labor starts helps lower the risk of infant exposure when viral suppression is not confirmed. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h5)

question: What is a major fear that stops patients from questioning healthcare providers?

options.A: Fear of paying extra taxes for medical equipment
options.B: Fear of being discharged without a diagnosis
options.C: Fear of retaliation or being neglected by staff
options.D: Fear that the medicine will expire too quickly

explanation: Correct! Patients often worry that if they complain or ask too many questions, the staff might treat them poorly or ignore them. [learn more](GNS122_U4_T7#GNS122_U4_T7_h5)

question: What must you check before giving a patient water after an upper GI scope?

options.A: That the patient's gag reflex has fully returned
options.B: That the patient's blood pressure is above normal
options.C: That the doctor has reviewed all laboratory results
options.D: That the patient has passed normal flatus

explanation: Their throat is usually numbed during the test. Checking for the gag reflex ensures they won't choke when they finally take a sip of water! [learn more](GNS221_U2_T2#GNS221_U2_T2_h6)

question: When you thoroughly wash your hands between patients in the ward, what are you mainly stopping?

options.A: It increases the resistance of the susceptible host.
options.B: It blocks the mode of transmission.
options.C: It destroys the natural reservoir of the pathogen.
options.D: It alters the portal of entry on the patient's skin.

explanation: Handwashing is your superpower! By washing your hands, you stop germs from hitching a ride from one patient to the next (blocking transmission). [learn more](GNS214_U1_T87#GNS214_U1_T87_h2)

question: When is it most important to routinely screen women for reproductive infections?

options.A: Whenever routine malaria testing is conducted
options.B: Only after the patient develops severe chronic pelvic pain
options.C: Strictly upon reaching forty years of age
options.D: During the first prenatal visit and for sexually active young adults

explanation: Early screening catches silent infections early, especially during pregnancy or in young adults before any lasting damage is done. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T4#GNS216_U5_T4_h4)

question: Why might an elderly patient talk about tummy aches and poor appetite instead of crying when they are grieving?

options.A: Older adults often express emotional pain through physical body complaints
options.B: Physical pain always replaces sadness in older people
options.C: Grief only affects the tummy and never the brain
options.D: They are just trying to get extra attention from the nurses

explanation: Spot on! Older adults often show emotional hurt through physical signs, known as somatic symptoms. Always keep an eye out for this in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T6#GNS221_U4_T6_h4)

question: What is the main reason conflict happens in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Having too many registered nurses on a single ward
options.B: Working an excessive number of consecutive night shifts
options.C: Strict adherence to hospital operational policies
options.D: A clash of values, goals, or needs between people

explanation: Conflict simply pops up when people interact and their personal values, goals, or needs don't match up. It happens to everyone, even the best healthcare teams! [learn more](GST321_U5_T1#GST321_U5_T1_h1)

question: What does medication adherence mean in nursing care?

options.A: How strictly a pharmacist follows doctor's prescription orders
options.B: How closely a patient follows their prescribed drug routine
options.C: The speed at which a drug dissolves in the stomach
options.D: The ability of a nurse to inject medications painlessly

explanation: Adherence checks whether the patient takes their drugs correctly regarding dose, time, and frequency. You're mastering core nursing terminology! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h6)

question: In a mass casualty incident, what does a RED triage tag mean?

options.A: Minor injuries that can wait until the end of the shift
options.B: Immediate life-threatening injuries with a high chance of survival
options.C: Injuries so severe that survival is unlikely
options.D: Deceased patients who need no further attention

explanation: Spot on! Red means urgent. It tells us the patient has a life-threatening problem that we can fix right now to save their life. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T4#GNS315_U5_T4_h2)

question: A child eats enough daily calories from starchy grains like maize or cassava, but still has severe anemia. What economic factor is likely behind this?

options.A: Too much household spending on medical insurance
options.B: Inability to afford protein and micronutrient-dense foods
options.C: High local agricultural productivity driving down grain value
options.D: Excessive availability of fresh vegetables in local markets

explanation: Getting enough calories for energy isn't the same as getting rich nutrients. Without money for protective foods, deficiencies like anemia happen. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T021#GNS227_U2_T021_h3)

question: How should a nurse talk to a patient about their use of local herbal mixtures to ensure safety?

options.A: Ignoring home remedies to focus solely on orthodox hospital drugs
options.B: Telling the patient immediately that all local herbs are dangerous poison
options.C: Reporting the patient to hospital security for using unapproved substances
options.D: Asking calm, non-judgmental questions about all home remedies used

explanation: Wonderful! Being open and non-judgmental builds trust, making patients feel safe to share what they are taking. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T10#GNS125_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which of the following measurements is included in anthropometric assessment?

options.A: Heart rate and rhythm
options.B: Serum albumin levels
options.C: Height and weight
options.D: Blood pressure readings

explanation: Anthropometric measurements involve physical body dimensions such as height, weight, and body mass index. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T001#GNS227_U2_T001_h6)

question: Why are fresh flowers and live plants banned from the room of an immunocompromised patient?

options.A: They attract stinging insects into the hospital room
options.B: Their soil and standing water harbor dangerous fungi
options.C: Their strong scent can trigger severe allergic asthma
options.D: They consume too much oxygen in a closed space

explanation: Soil and stagnant water are breeding grounds for fungi and bacteria that can easily cause severe infections in patients with low white blood cells. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h3)

question: A shortage of which mineral leads to an enlarged thyroid gland, known as a goiter?

options.A: Iodine
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Iron
options.D: Zinc

explanation: You got it! Iodine helps the thyroid gland make important hormones. Without enough iodine, the thyroid swells up, causing a goiter. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T7#GNS313_U3_T7_h2)

question: What is the main lab test used to find parasite eggs in clinic patients?

options.A: Taking an X-ray of the chest cavity
options.B: Microscopic stool examination
options.C: Performing a standard throat swab culture
options.D: Measuring routine fasting blood glucose

explanation: Lab techs look at prepared stool samples under a microscope to spot the unique shapes of parasite eggs. Perfect! [learn more](GST114_U3_T8#GST114_U3_T8_h6)

question: Why do nurses need to understand workplace hazards?

options.A: To calculate company profits
options.B: To diagnose every non-work illness in the community
options.C: To help prevent both sudden injuries and long-term illnesses
options.D: To replace the factory safety manager

explanation: As nurses, knowing about workplace hazards helps us protect workers, advocate for their safety, and stop health issues before they even start! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T5#GNS225_U7_T5_h1)

question: Why does a patient not feel pain when a surgeon touches the actual brain tissue during a procedure?

options.A: Anesthesia freezes all nerves permanently
options.B: The brain tissue lacks pain receptors
options.C: The skull blocks pain signals from escaping
options.D: The dura mater numbs the rest of the brain

explanation: Because brain tissue has no nociceptors, pain is only felt when surrounding structures like the scalp, blood vessels, or meninges are irritated. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T3#GNS211_U3_T3_h2)

question: A research group finds a questionnaire that was super reliable in the US ten years ago. Why must they test its reliability again for a new local study?

options.A: Hospital ethics committees require a new test to pay the researchers
options.B: Published research papers automatically expire after five years
options.C: Cultural differences and demographics can change how the tool performs
options.D: Statistical formulas change every decade to match new computer systems

explanation: Reliability isn't a permanent stamp of approval. A tool that works great in one culture or setting might need re-testing to prove it fits a different local population. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h7)

question: What part of the female reproductive system does a vulval tumour affect?

options.A: The external female genitalia
options.B: The glandular tissue of the cervix
options.C: The inner lining of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The muscular wall of the uterus

explanation: Vulval tumours specifically develop on the external structures of the female genitalia, such as the labia and clitoris. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h1)

question: Which Nigerian agency is well known for regulating food and drug safety?

options.A: JAMB
options.B: NAFDAC
options.C: NYSC
options.D: FRSC

explanation: NAFDAC (National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control) is our main regulatory body for food and drugs in Nigeria. Proudly Nigerian nursing knowledge! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h6)

question: Why do doctors prescribe anticholinergic medications for urinary symptoms?

options.A: To relax the bladder and increase holding capacity
options.B: To kill bacteria causing urinary tract infections
options.C: To shrink an enlarged prostate gland
options.D: To stimulate bladder contractions during voiding

explanation: These drugs stop the bladder from going into sudden spasms, meaning your patient can hold more urine without that emergency rush to the toilet. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T5#GNS223_U8_T5_h1)

question: What is the minimum recommended time for washing hands with soap and water?

options.A: 20 seconds
options.B: 2 minutes
options.C: 10 seconds
options.D: 5 seconds

explanation: Washing for at least 20 seconds gives friction and soap enough time to mechanically remove and destroy transient microorganisms. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h5)

question: Why do disaster survivors often experience severe psychological distress alongside physical injuries?

options.A: Because the sudden event shatters their sense of safety and security
options.B: Because medication given in hospitals always causes anxiety
options.C: Because disaster victims rarely have family members nearby
options.D: Because physical pain stops the brain from thinking clearly

explanation: Disasters violently disrupt the predictable routines and safety nets that people rely on to feel secure in the world. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h1)

question: A patient arrives with a massive pulmonary embolism. What is happening in their body?

options.A: Blood flow through the pulmonary arteries is blocked, impairing oxygenation
options.B: The liver has stopped producing clotting factors, causing widespread bleeding
options.C: An infection in the urinary tract has spread into the spinal fluid
options.D: Gastric acid is leaking directly into the peritoneal cavity through an ulcer

explanation: A pulmonary embolism is a blocked blood vessel in the lungs. Because the blockage is there, blood can't pick up fresh oxygen to circulate. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why do we only use glutaraldehyde on medical equipment instead of human skin?

options.A: It turns the skin bright yellow for several weeks.
options.B: It is a high-level disinfectant that releases toxic fumes and irritates skin.
options.C: It instantly evaporates when it touches human skin.
options.D: It only works when it is mixed with hot boiling water.

explanation: That's right! Glutaraldehyde is extremely harsh and gives off strong fumes, so it belongs in soaking tanks for instruments, never on a patient's skin. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T10#GNS215_U6_T10_h3)

question: Why do nurses study anatomy and physiology together?

options.A: Pathology cannot occur without simultaneous changes in both areas
options.B: How an organ is built directly shapes how it does its job
options.C: Medical equipment is built based strictly on anatomical dimensions
options.D: It is a strict requirement for passing hospital licensing exams

explanation: You've got this! Structure and function always go hand in hand. An organ's physical shape is specially designed to make its everyday job possible. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T1#GNS111_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why are regular walkthrough inspections so important for an occupational health nurse?

options.A: To discipline workers who fail to wear proper uniforms
options.B: To check the financial profits of the plant
options.C: To replace safety officers during their annual leave
options.D: To observe daily work tasks and identify unaddressed environmental risks

explanation: Exactly! Walking through the workspace lets you spot hidden dangers that workers might just get used to and forget to report. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T3#GNS225_U7_T3_h4)

question: What is the term for the grating sound heard when broken bone ends rub together?

options.A: Cyanosis
options.B: Contracture
options.C: Crepitus
options.D: Clonus

explanation: Crepitus is the distinctive crunchy sound or sensation produced when rough ends of fractured bone rub together. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T13#GNS221_U3_T13_h3)

question: What is the main focus of occupational therapy for individuals with degenerative disorders?

options.A: Performing complex neurological surgeries
options.B: Providing formal psychological counseling
options.C: Assisting with daily activities like dressing and eating
options.D: Managing prescription medication schedules

explanation: Occupational therapists are experts at helping patients maintain independence in personal care and household tasks through smart adaptations. Great job! [learn more](GNS222_U4_T17#GNS222_U4_T17_h5)

question: What is the final step after completing a thorough research critique?

options.A: Firing staff members who do not read journals
options.B: Writing a textbook about research methods
options.C: Throwing away the article because all studies have flaws
options.D: Deciding whether the evidence is strong enough to change clinical practice

explanation: The ultimate purpose of nursing research critique is to determine if and how the findings can safely improve patient care. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h6)

question: How do most drugs travel from a pregnant mother to her baby?

options.A: Direct swallowing of amniotic fluid
options.B: Filtration through the fetal kidneys
options.C: Active pumping by the umbilical cord
options.D: Simple diffusion across the placenta

explanation: Medicines in the mother's bloodstream mostly cross over the placenta easily through simple diffusion to reach the baby. You've got this! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T5#GNS215_U6_T5_h1)

question: What medication is given immediately to reverse a heparin overdose?

options.A: Protamine sulfate
options.B: Vitamin K tablets
options.C: Fresh whole blood
options.D: Calcium gluconate

explanation: Protamine sulfate is the fast-acting antidote that neutralizes heparin right away in an emergency. You're doing amazing! [learn more](GNS215_U6_T14#GNS215_U6_T14_h7)

question: How is a double-contrast barium enema different from a single-contrast study?

options.A: It takes pictures of the small intestine rather than the large colon
options.B: It uses an oral contrast liquid instead of going through the rectum
options.C: It uses both liquid barium and air to highlight fine details on the bowel wall
options.D: It requires surgical anesthesia while the single contrast needs only local numbing

explanation: Adding air alongside the barium gives a thin, clear coating to the inner walls. This helps doctors spot tiny polyps or early signs of inflammation easily. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T9#GNS212_U1_T9_h1)

question: What protective action prevents food from entering the respiratory airway during a normal swallow?

options.A: The tongue pushes forward to close off the esophagus
options.B: The vocal cords tighten to block all airflow permanently
options.C: The epiglottis folds down to cover the larynx
options.D: The hard palate drops down to seal the pharynx

explanation: During swallowing, the epiglottis acts like a lid, flipping downward to shield the airway and guide food safely into the esophagus. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T1#GNS121_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why are 4th-generation HIV tests that check for p24 antigens so helpful for early diagnosis?

options.A: They detect viral proteins before the body even finishes making antibodies.
options.B: They require no blood drawing and use only routine urine samples.
options.C: They can distinguish between HIV-1 and HIV-2 with 100% certainty instantly.
options.D: They completely eliminate the need for any follow-up confirmatory testing.

explanation: Checking for antigens lets us catch the virus early, even before antibodies show up. Brilliant concept to master! [learn more](GNS216_U6_T1#GNS216_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which of the following is an example of an adaptive coping mechanism for a newly diagnosed HIV patient?

options.A: Turning to heavy alcohol use to forget the diagnosis
options.B: Denying the existence of the virus and skipping clinic visits
options.C: Joining a peer support group and talking with a counsellor
options.D: Isolating oneself completely from all human contact

explanation: Seeking community support and professional guidance helps patients process their diagnosis in a healthy, constructive manner. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T8#GNS216_U6_T8_h7)

question: Which part of the teenage brain develops early and drives strong emotions and the search for excitement?

options.A: The cerebellum
options.B: The occipital lobe
options.C: The prefrontal cortex
options.D: The limbic system

explanation: You got this! The limbic system matures early in adolescence, making emotions intense and driving reward-seeking before the brain's rational control center is fully grown. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T7#GNS312_U3_T7_h1)

question: What is the primary purpose of the nasal conchae or turbinates on the lateral wall?

options.A: To trap large dust particles directly at the external nares
options.B: To produce tears that lubricate the nasal mucosa
options.C: To create turbulent airflow and increase surface area
options.D: To house the specialized receptors for the sense of taste

explanation: The curvy shape of the conchae forces air to swirl around, maximizing contact with the warm, moist lining so it gets conditioned properly. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h2)

question: What is the primary maternal function of human chorionic gonadotropin in early pregnancy?

options.A: To stimulate milk production in maternal breast tissue
options.B: To lower maternal blood pressure for fetal protection
options.C: To trigger the immediate onset of active labour contractions
options.D: To stimulate the corpus luteum to produce progesterone

explanation: hCG signals the corpus luteum to keep producing progesterone early on, which protects and maintains the uterine lining until the placenta can take over that job. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h1)

question: Why do a community diagnosis before starting an IEC campaign?

options.A: Identify the actual health burdens affecting the local population
options.B: Prove that the community lacks basic hygiene practices
options.C: Fulfill administrative paperwork requirements for the local government
options.D: Determine how many nurses are needed for night duty shifts

explanation: You got it! Just like assessing an individual patient before treatment, a community diagnosis helps you find out what health issues are truly troubling the people. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T2#GNS214_U1_T2_h2)

question: What do we call it when a hospital ward slowly slips back into old, messy habits after an improvement project finishes?

options.A: Systemic clinical drift
options.B: Relapse to old ways
options.C: Forcing function failure
options.D: Special cause variation

explanation: It's easy to slide back into comfort zones! That's why keeping new habits alive requires ongoing teamwork and support. [learn more](GST319_U2_T2#GST319_U2_T2_h6)

question: Why is it dangerous to place a septic drain field too close to a shallow drinking water well?

options.A: Roots from nearby trees will block the water pipes completely
options.B: Liquid effluent can seep into the groundwater and spread pathogens
options.C: The weight of the water well can crush the underground septic tank
options.D: The smell of the drain field will ruin the taste of the well water

explanation: If a drain field is too close to a well, untreated wastewater can travel through the soil and contaminate the underground drinking water with dangerous bacteria and viruses. [learn more](GST114_U6_T4#GST114_U6_T4_h4)

question: Why is a multidisciplinary team necessary for managing advanced chronic pain?

options.A: Pain touches physical, emotional, and social aspects requiring diverse expertise
options.B: Nurses cannot assess pain intensity without a physiotherapist present
options.C: Doctors are not legally allowed to prescribe pain medicine without a pharmacist
options.D: Hospital accreditation rules require at least five professionals on every chart

explanation: Because total pain affects body, mind, and spirit, a team of medical, nursing, social, and spiritual experts provides the best comprehensive care. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h8)

question: Why is it important for a primary health nurse to understand local traditional health beliefs?

options.A: It proves that traditional practices are always superior to science
options.B: It allows the nurse to replace all modern medicine with herbs
options.C: It stops patients from ever visiting local herbalists
options.D: It helps build trust and improves cooperation with medical treatments

explanation: Respecting traditional views helps nurses bridge the gap between community practices and safe, evidence-based health care. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h5)

question: What does it mean when a disease is described as 'endemic' in a community?

options.A: It only affects travellers visiting from foreign countries
options.B: It appears once every ten years and then vanishes
options.C: It is constantly present at a steady baseline level
options.D: It suddenly affects people across multiple continents

explanation: Think of an endemic disease as a constant visitor—it stays within a specific area consistently over time without needing a fresh introduction from outside. You've got this! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T88#GNS214_U1_T88_h1)

question: What structural feature makes capillaries ideally suited for gas and nutrient exchange?

options.A: They are equipped with one-way valves to prevent backflow
options.B: Their walls are only a single cell layer thick
options.C: They contain strong layers of circular smooth muscle
options.D: Their lumen has a larger diameter than any other vessel

explanation: Having a wall thickness of just one cell minimizes the diffusion distance for oxygen, nutrients, and waste products. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T5#GNS111_U2_T5_h3)

question: How are most deep placental problems, like placenta accreta, usually spotted before delivery?

options.A: Measuring maternal blood pressure twice daily
options.B: Performing a routine digital cervical examination
options.C: Routine antenatal ultrasound and color Doppler imaging
options.D: Testing maternal blood hormone levels every week

explanation: Ultrasound with Doppler scans lets doctors look right at how the blood vessels are behaving before labor even starts. No guesswork needed! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h6)

question: Why is continuous emotional reassurance important during intra-natal care?

options.A: It replaces the need for physical monitoring of the fetus
options.B: It forces the cervix to dilate much faster
options.C: It lowers anxiety and helps the mother cope with labor pain
options.D: It completely stops the progression of strong contractions

explanation: Emotional support reduces fear and stress hormones, which helps the mother manage the intense physical demands of labor more effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T50#GNS214_U1_T50_h1)

question: Which tiny creature carries the Guinea worm larvae before a human drinks them?

options.A: Cyclops water flea
options.B: Tsetse fly
options.C: Anopheles mosquito
options.D: Freshwater snail

explanation: Well done! Tiny water fleas called cyclops swallow the larvae, and people accidentally ingest them by drinking unfiltered water. Every question you answer makes you a sharper nurse! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h2)

question: Why is feeling deeply distressed after a disaster considered a normal human reaction?

options.A: Because everyone experiences identical symptoms of grief
options.B: Because human brains are wired to ignore sudden changes
options.C: Because the event itself is abnormal and threatening to safety
options.D: Because medical treatment is rarely needed for shock

explanation: Spot on! It is completely normal to feel distressed when something terrifying and life-threatening happens around you. Your mind and body are just trying to process the shock. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T3#GNS314_U6_T3_h1)

question: Why is pregnancy in young adolescents considered a higher medical risk?

options.A: It completely stops the normal growth of the infant's internal organs
options.B: It prevents breast milk production entirely after delivery
options.C: It guarantees that the mother will develop chronic heart disease later in life
options.D: It increases the likelihood of complications like premature birth and high blood pressure

explanation: You nailed it! Young bodies are still growing themselves, which raises the chances of issues like high blood pressure during pregnancy and early delivery. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T19#GNS312_U3_T19_h6)

question: When you are taking a family health history, which group of relatives should you focus on first?

options.A: Neighbors living in the same community
options.B: Colleagues and close personal friends
options.C: First-degree relatives like parents and siblings
options.D: Distant cousins and second-degree relatives

explanation: You nailed it! Parents, brothers, and sisters share the closest genetic traits with your patient, so their medical history matters most. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a direct job of an antibody?

options.A: Direct phagocytosis of pathogens by the antibody itself
options.B: Activation of the complement system
options.C: Agglutination of floating foreign cells
options.D: Neutralization of harmful bacterial toxins

explanation: Antibodies don't swallow germs themselves—they act like detectives and taggers. They leave the actual eating (phagocytosis) to specialized cells like macrophages! [learn more](GST114_U4_T3#GST114_U4_T3_h4)

question: A patient is admitted with right-sided heart failure. Which physical sign is the nurse most likely to spot?

options.A: Flushed, warm skin and bounding pulses
options.B: Sudden high fever and severe headache
options.C: Bulging neck veins and swollen ankles
options.D: Clear lung sounds with no breathing trouble

explanation: Right-sided failure causes fluid to back up into the rest of the body. You'll often see this as swollen legs and distended neck veins! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T12#GNS213_U1_T12_h7)

question: What electrical change happens inside the cell to spark a smell signal?

options.A: An influx of sodium and calcium ions into the cell
options.B: A sudden drop in cyclic AMP levels
options.C: The direct breakdown of protein molecules
options.D: A massive outflow of potassium ions

explanation: Correct! When ion channels open, positively charged sodium and calcium ions rush inside the cell. This change in electrical charge creates an impulse that travels up to the brain. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T9#GNS211_U4_T9_h3)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do with a mechanical weighing scale before a patient steps on it?

options.A: Wipe the platform with hot cooking oil
options.B: Place a thick mat underneath it
options.C: Lock the height rod permanently
options.D: Calibrate and balance it to zero

explanation: Always check that the scale starts right at zero! This ensures your weight reading is accurate and not thrown off by a previous reading. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T3#GNS112_U6_T3_h2)

question: How should you position a patient right after a craniotomy surgery to help keep intracranial pressure down?

options.A: Sitting upright at a 90-degree angle
options.B: Flat on the back with feet raised high
options.C: Head elevated 30 to 45 degrees
options.D: Lying flat on the operative side

explanation: Excellent clinical thinking! Elevating the head of the bed helps blood flow smoothly out of the head (venous return), preventing fluid backup and keeping pressure low. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T14#GNS222_U3_T14_h6)

question: What is the main job of the skin's natural lipids (fats) found between skin cells?

options.A: They fight off local germs like your body's immune system
options.B: They make skin pigment to block the sun's rays
options.C: They give the deeper skin layer its stretch and bounce
options.D: They act like mortar to lock in moisture and keep germs out

explanation: Think of skin cells like bricks and these lipids like the mortar between them. This oily seal keeps your hydration locked in and prevents harmful invaders from entering. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T7#GNS213_U5_T7_h1)

question: A nurse gets a positive rapid malaria test for a pregnant woman in a remote village. What should happen next?

options.A: Tell her to return home and wait for the fever to disappear on its own
options.B: Initiate the appropriate anti-malarial treatment protocol immediately
options.C: Ignore the result because rapid tests are never accurate
options.D: Send her patient file directly to the international health organization

explanation: Testing is only helpful if we act on the results! Once malaria is confirmed, starting treatment right away keeps both mother and baby safe. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T7#GNS124_U6_T7_h5)

question: A community nurse notices a sudden spike in typhoid cases in a village. What is the best first move?

options.A: Close all schools in the country permanently
options.B: Order immediate quarantine for every healthy person in the region
options.C: Stop all routine vaccinations until the investigation ends
options.D: Investigate potential sources like local water supplies and food handlers

explanation: To stop an outbreak, you have to play detective! Tracking down contaminated water or food handlers helps you find the exact source. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T3#GNS313_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is keeping the head of a ventilated patient's bed elevated at 30 to 45 degrees such an important nursing action?

options.A: Endotracheal tube cuff rupture
options.B: Diaphragmatic muscle atrophy
options.C: Ventilator-associated pneumonia
options.D: Barotrauma from high tidal volumes

explanation: Gravity is our friend here! Elevating the bed stops oral and stomach fluids from pooling above the tube cuff and trickling down into the lungs to cause pneumonia. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T18#GNS213_U2_T18_h6)

question: What is another popular name for an admission bed in the ward?

options.A: Cardiac bed
options.B: Open bed
options.C: Fracture bed
options.D: Closed bed

explanation: That's right! We call it an open bed because the top covers are folded back nicely to welcome the new patient. [learn more](GNS112_U4_T3#GNS112_U4_T3_h3)

question: In nursing and public health, what does the acronym IEC stand for?

options.A: Intervention, Education, and Control
options.B: Immunization, Evaluation, and Care
options.C: Infection, Environment, and Community
options.D: Information, Education, and Communication

explanation: IEC stands for Information, Education, and Communication. These are the three core pillars we use in community health to share healthy habits and ideas! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T6#GNS124_U5_T6_h1)

question: A nurse manager creates a ward schedule that requires double the current nursing staff, ignoring the hospital budget. Which principle of planning was violated?

options.A: Continuity
options.B: Flexibility
options.C: Feasibility
options.D: Secrecy

explanation: Feasibility means a plan must be realistic and work within actual available resources like budgets and staff numbers. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h2)

question: What was Paul Ehrlich searching for with his idea of a 'magic bullet'?

options.A: To invent a vaccine that prevents all known viral infections with a single dose
options.B: To find a chemical that targets and destroys pathogens while sparing the human host
options.C: To prove that bad air is the primary cause of wound infections in surgery
options.D: To design a high-powered microscope lens that magnifies living viruses

explanation: The magic bullet is all about selective toxicity—wiping out the bad germs without poisoning the patient's healthy cells. [learn more](GST114_U1_T2#GST114_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is the most important advice for a patient who just received IV contrast dye?

options.A: Stay strictly in bed for the next two days
options.B: Take a strong antibiotic pill
options.C: Avoid eating any protein for the rest of the day
options.D: Drink plenty of fluids to help flush the dye out

explanation: Drinking water helps the kidneys wash the contrast dye out of the body quickly and safely. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T8#GNS222_U3_T8_h8)

question: What is the main goal of providing nutrition care for patients in the hospital?

options.A: Preventing malnutrition and supporting healing
options.B: Reducing the cost of hospital food services
options.C: Replacing the need for doctor-ordered diets
options.D: Ensuring patients gain weight during every stay

explanation: Great job! Good nutrition keeps the body strong so it can fight off infections and heal wounds faster. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h1)

question: How do nurses determine if a specific disease rate in a community is a serious problem?

options.A: By waiting for international agencies to declare an emergency
options.B: By checking how many doctors are currently on duty
options.C: By comparing local rates with regional or national standards
options.D: By asking traditional healers for their personal opinions

explanation: Comparing local health data against established benchmarks helps nurses identify which conditions require urgent public health attention. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T5#GNS124_U3_T5_h4)

question: Besides cancer, what other health problem are cytotoxic drugs often used to treat?

options.A: Acute vitamin deficiencies
options.B: Severe autoimmune disorders
options.C: Degenerative bone diseases
options.D: Bacterial respiratory infections

explanation: Correct! Because they calm down overactive cells, these drugs are also helpful for conditions like severe arthritis or lupus. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T7#GNS215_U6_T7_h3)

question: Which of these common phrases should a nurse avoid saying to someone who is grieving?

options.A: I am here for you whenever you want to talk
options.B: I am so sorry for your loss
options.C: Time heals all wounds
options.D: It is okay to cry if you need to

explanation: Phrases like 'time heals all wounds' can feel dismissive and unhelpful. Instead, just let them know you are there for them. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T6#GNS221_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the main reason hospitals use standardized usability questionnaires for electronic health records?

options.A: To test the speed of the hospital internet server cables
options.B: To measure user satisfaction and ease of use in a structured way
options.C: To calculate the financial budget for buying new computers
options.D: To check if the computer hardware is physically clean

explanation: Exactly! These questionnaires give hospitals a clear, reliable score on whether their software is actually user-friendly for nurses. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T2#GNS113_U3_T2_h5)

question: Why is it a drawback to keep a successful quality project locked inside just one nursing unit?

options.A: It prevents other patients and staff from benefiting from proven safer practices
options.B: It causes the original unit to lose funding for their nursing supplies
options.C: It automatically violates hospital licensing and accreditation standards
options.D: It forces the hospital to hire extra consultants from outside the country

explanation: Sharing is caring in nursing! When we keep great improvements hidden in one ward, other patients miss out on safer care. [learn more](GST319_U1_T6#GST319_U1_T6_h1)

question: A patient experiences a sudden drop in systemic blood pressure. Which vessel directly supplies blood into the glomerulus for filtration?

options.A: Efferent arteriole
options.B: Afferent arteriole
options.C: Peritubular capillary
options.D: Interlobular vein

explanation: The afferent arteriole brings blood directly into the glomerular capillary bed to generate the pressure needed for filtration. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h3)

question: How much food should you put on the spoon when feeding an adult patient?

options.A: Just a single tiny drop
options.B: One-third to one-half full
options.C: Overflowing with extra gravy
options.D: Packed tightly to the very top

explanation: Smaller spoonfuls are much easier and safer for the patient to chew and swallow without getting overwhelmed. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T3#GNS212_U1_T3_h4)

question: What does an endemic disease mean in a community?

options.A: An outbreak that affects only travellers arriving from overseas
options.B: A rare condition that has been completely eradicated by vaccines
options.C: A disease that is constantly present at a predictable baseline level
options.D: A sudden wave of infections that spreads across multiple countries

explanation: An endemic disease maintains a steady, predictable presence within a specific population rather than appearing as a sudden unexpected wave. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h1)

question: Why must a nurse wash their hands immediately after removing gloves?

options.A: Gloves can have tiny invisible defects and hands can become contaminated during removal
options.B: Soap helps preserve the natural oils in the skin of the hands
options.C: Hospital policy requires handwashing only before putting on gloves
options.D: It removes any lingering powder left inside the glove material

explanation: Microscopic leaks or accidental contamination during glove stripping means hands are rarely completely clean underneath. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T8#GNS313_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why do hospital cleaners and nurses wipe down bed rails and bedside tables so often?

options.A: Air currents deposit airborne droplets directly onto these objects
options.B: Patients spend most of their recovery time touching these areas
options.C: Microorganisms multiply rapidly on metal surfaces without moisture
options.D: These surfaces act as common fomites for indirect contact spread

explanation: Exactly! High-touch areas easily collect germs from hands and pass them along to the next person, which is why cleaning them stops indirect spread. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h2)

question: In Herzberg's theory, what is the main job of 'hygiene factors' like basic pay and a clean workplace?

options.A: Guarantees that every worker will achieve self-actualization
options.B: Determining which clinical nurses receive a promotion
options.C: Preventing job dissatisfaction rather than creating deep motivation
options.D: Replacing the need for monetary compensation in public hospitals

explanation: Hygiene factors stop people from complaining (like fixing a broken fan or paying salaries on time), but true job love comes from other things like feeling valued. [learn more](GST321_U1_T18#GST321_U1_T18_h3)

question: Which medication group requires careful review before a pacemaker insertion due to bleeding risks?

options.A: Anticoagulants
options.B: Antihistamines
options.C: Antacids
options.D: Antibiotics

explanation: Blood thinners increase the risk of bleeding into the surgical pocket where the pacemaker battery is placed. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T9#GNS321_U2_T9_h3)

question: Which bloodborne viruses are most commonly transmitted through unsafe injection practices?

options.A: Malaria, Typhoid, and Cholera
options.B: Influenza, Measles, and Chickenpox
options.C: Tetanus, Rabies, and Yellow Fever
options.D: Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV

explanation: Unsafe injections are a major vector for transmitting bloodborne infections like Hepatitis B, Hepatitis C, and HIV. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h4)

question: During a building collapse, a nurse finds a victim who is unresponsive, not breathing even after opening the airway, and has no pulse. What triage tag should they get?

options.A: Green (Walking Wounded)
options.B: Red (Immediate)
options.C: Yellow (Delayed)
options.D: Black (Expectant / Deceased)

explanation: This is a tough call in mass casualty triage, but a black tag is used when injuries are so severe that resuscitation is impossible, allowing us to focus on survivors. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h7)

question: What visual acuity score in the better eye (even with glasses) is generally used to define legal blindness?

options.A: 20/70 or worse
options.B: 20/40 or worse
options.C: 20/100 or worse
options.D: 20/200 or worse

explanation: You've got this! Legal blindness is officially classified as having a corrected visual acuity of 20/200 or lower in the better eye. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T13#GNS324_U4_T13_h1)

question: Reviewing existing clinic registers and local government health reports is an example of which data collection method?

options.A: Experimental data collection
options.B: Secondary data collection
options.C: Primary data collection
options.D: Biological data collection

explanation: Using already recorded data from registers and reports is classed as secondary data because it was collected by someone else previously. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h2)

question: Which type of quality measure looks directly at the final clinical result or health status of a patient?

options.A: Process measure
options.B: Outcome measure
options.C: Balancing measure
options.D: Financial measure

explanation: Spot on! Outcome measures check the final destination—like whether the patient's infection cleared up or how well they are recovering. [learn more](GST319_U2_T1#GST319_U2_T1_h5)

question: What does the presence of normal peristaltic stripping waves indicate in the esophagus?

options.A: An abnormal blockage trapping fluid inside the upper chest
options.B: A complete failure of the lower esophageal sphincter to relax
options.C: The presence of a large sliding hiatal hernia in the hiatus
options.D: Coordinated muscle contractions pushing food and contrast downward

explanation: Peristaltic waves are the rhythmic muscular squeezes of the esophagus that successfully clear the barium bolus into the stomach. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h5)

question: Why must school management set aside specific funds in their yearly budget for health?

options.A: To purchase luxury furniture for administrative offices
options.B: To pay for students' personal family medical bills
options.C: To purchase medical supplies and maintain health facilities
options.D: To fund international educational excursions

explanation: You nailed it! Having dedicated funds means first-aid items, cleaning products, and clinic tools are always ready when emergencies happen. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T4#GNS225_U4_T4_h4)

question: What is the safe temperature range for storing routine vaccines like Pentavalent and PCV in a clinic refrigerator?

options.B: +2°C to +8°C

explanation: Routine diluents and liquid vaccines like Pentavalent and PCV must be kept cool between two and eight degrees Celsius and never frozen. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T61#GNS214_U1_T61_h5)

question: What is the primary focus of pediatric palliative and hospice care at home?

question: What is the main ethical dilemma when managing patients on psychiatric parole?

question: What is the normal, healthy look of a newly made intestinal stoma?

question: In nursing, what is a 'fomite'?

question: Why do vitamin and mineral shortages happen so easily in people living with HIV?

options.D: Because they drink too much clean water

question: Why is a nurse's daily report on how much a patient ate so helpful to the dietitian?

options.C: It helps the dietitian evaluate if nutritional targets are met

question: What is the primary purpose of an adult day care home?

options.D: To provide daytime supervised care and support services

question: Why does fetal hemoglobin take up oxygen so effectively from maternal blood in the placenta?

question: What is a major benefit of Tai Chi for older adults at risk of falling?

options.A: It rapidly increases total body bone density

options.D: It cures chronic joint inflammation in the knees

question: In a nursing research study, what does the independent variable stand for?

options.D: The presumed cause or experimental intervention being tested

question: A rescue team is about to free a trapped miner whose legs were under rubble for hours. What critical medical step must nurses prepare for?

options.A: Preparing the patient for immediate general anesthesia in the field
options.B: Withholding all fluids to prevent severe pulmonary edema
options.C: Applying a tight tourniquet to every limb before any movement starts
options.D: Administering large volumes of intravenous fluids to prevent kidney failure

explanation: Spot on! When trapped limbs are freed, toxins rush into the bloodstream. IV fluids help flush these out before they can shut down the kidneys. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h3)

question: An unresponsive patient is brought in. After you make sure their airway and breathing are okay, what is your next immediate step?

options.A: Inquiring about dietary preferences for hospital meals

options.C: Reviewing the patient's employment history and workplace

question: What does zoonotic spillover mean in the context of infectious diseases?

options.C: Chemical waste spills into rivers and poisons aquatic life
options.D: Pathogens jump from animals to infect human populations

explanation: Zoonotic spillover occurs when infectious agents living in animal hosts cross the barrier to infect humans. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h2)

question: Why do nurses inject a little bit of air into a closed medication vial before pulling out the liquid?

options.A: To increase the potency of the drug

options.C: To prevent a vacuum and ease withdrawal
options.D: To sterilize the rubber stopper surface

question: What is the medical term for infective bone disease?

options.A: Osteoarthritis

options.C: Osteomyelitis

explanation: Osteomyelitis is the specific term used to describe an infection and inflammation of the bone and bone marrow. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T17#GNS222_U1_T17_h1)

question: Why can it be extra challenging to build trust with patients who have illness anxiety?

question: Which of these is NOT a daily job for a nurse in infection control?

question: Why do teenagers often take sudden risks even when they know the dangers?

options.A: They deliberately ignore all forms of social interaction

options.C: They possess completely adult-like cognitive maturity in all situations
options.D: Their neurological risk assessment and impulse control circuits are still maturing

question: Which cranial nerve brings most of the sensory messages from our entire face?

question: Which part of the hand is best to use when checking a patient's skin temperature?

options.A: The knuckles

question: A patient with a history of epilepsy comes to the clinic reporting frequent seizures after spending a week studying all night for exams. Which trigger is most likely responsible?

options.A: Genetic mutation
options.B: Flashing lights
options.C: Sleep deprivation
options.D: Cerebral infection

question: How do the speaker and screen on an AED help you during an emergency?

options.A: They record the conversation between family members and healthcare providers.

options.C: They display the patient's exact medical history and home medications.

question: Which of the following is linked as an environmental trigger for developing MS?

question: What does 'validity' mean when we talk about a research checklist?

question: How does health insurance make it easier for people to get medical care?

options.A: By making all drugs and lab tests completely free to manufacture

question: What is the main reason infectious waste is shredded after going through microwave treatment?

options.C: To separate plastic components from metal parts manually

question: Which specific hormone surge directly triggers the release of the egg from the ovary?

question: How do long-acting injectable antipsychotics make community care easier?

question: Where are surgical family planning procedures, like tubal ligation, usually performed?

question: How should a nurse handle it when a patient's cultural beliefs tell them to avoid certain healthy foods?

question: What is the main goal of maternal home healthcare visits in our communities?

question: Why do we say a resident's care plan must be treated as a living document?

question: When helping a stroke patient with left-sided weakness put on a button-down shirt, which arm goes in first?

question: What usually happens to the endocrine functions of the kidneys when renal tissue becomes damaged?

question: What is an important way community health nurses can help prevent FGM?

question: What should a nurse leader do if given an administrative order that breaks nursing ethics?

question: How soon after getting the yellow fever vaccine does protective immunity usually kick in?

question: Which of the following is an example of a quantitative indicator used to evaluate community mobilisation?

question: Why is a continuous supply of nutrients necessary for human tissues?

question: What is the primary function of the transverse pontine fibers?

question: What is the primary difference between hearing and active listening?

question: Who is famous for introducing the 'total pain' concept in palliative care?

question: How has Nigeria's federal budget allocation for health traditionally compared to the Abuja target?

question: Why do smartphones and social media apps increase the risk of early unprotected sex?

question: A nurse wants to read a new study, but the journal website demands a heavy payment to view it. What kind of barrier is this?

question: During a home visit, the nurse sees loose scatter rugs on the floor. What is the best advice?

question: What happens inside the eye when a person reads a book held close to their face?

question: When must a nurse choose soap and water instead of an alcohol hand rub?

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the emergency ABCDE assessment framework?

question: Why are gravies and sauces often added to meats on a soft diet?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common reason why infections cause nutrient depletion?

question: A nurse is getting ready to give activated charcoal to a patient who swallowed poison. Which of these actions is a dangerous mistake?

question: A patient arrives at the emergency unit in status epilepticus (a seizure that won't stop). Which drug class should be given immediately to halt it?

question: How is the care for a stable patient with a bruised heart (contusion) different from someone with a bleeding heart wound?

question: Why do community health nurses spend time educating the public?

question: Who counts as a food handler in public health?

options.C: Factory workers who manufacture food packaging materials
options.D: Anyone who touches food, equipment, or food contact surfaces

explanation: Anyone who comes into direct contact with food, cooking tools, or preparation surfaces during their work is considered a food handler. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U7_T007#GNS227_U7_T007_h1)

question: What are the core checks to perform during a neurovascular assessment of a limb in traction?

options.A: Joint range, breath sounds, and pulses
options.B: Pain scale, pin length, and skin turgor
options.C: Circulation, motion, and sensation
options.D: Temperature, weight, and muscle tone

explanation: You nailed it! Always remember the ABCs of neurovascular checks: checking if blood is flowing (circulation), if they can move (motion), and if they can feel (sensation). [learn more](GNS221_U1_T9#GNS221_U1_T9_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a limitation or challenge of healthcare simulation?

options.A: Fitting simulation hours into a packed curriculum is difficult
options.B: Instructors need specialized training to run advanced scenarios properly
options.C: Mannequins cannot fully duplicate every emotional nuance of a real patient
options.D: Simulation successfully improves teamwork and reduces medical errors

explanation: Improving teamwork and reducing errors is a major benefit of simulation, not a limitation or challenge. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h7)

question: What exactly is a 'biphasic' anaphylactic reaction?

options.A: A mild skin rash that turns into severe breathing difficulty within minutes
options.B: A sudden allergic response that only affects the skin and digestive system
options.C: A return of symptoms hours after the initial attack without new allergen exposure
options.D: An allergic reaction triggered by two different foods at the exact same time

explanation: A biphasic reaction is like a sneaky second wave. Symptoms come back hours later even though the patient had no new contact with the trigger. [learn more](GST114_U4_T9#GST114_U4_T9_h6)

question: What is the very first step of the nursing process when caring for a patient?

options.A: Assessment
options.B: Prescription
options.C: Implementation
options.D: Evaluation

explanation: You got it! Assessment is where you gather all the important details about your patient's health before planning any care. [learn more](GST321_U8_T7#GST321_U8_T7_h5)

question: A hospital manager checks patient charts to see if a new pain relief guide is working well. What goal does this support?

options.A: Patient self-monitoring of symptoms
options.B: Personal communication between doctors
options.C: Immediate bedside nursing handover
options.D: Quality improvement and research

explanation: Correct! Looking back at charts helps the hospital find ways to upgrade patient care and nursing protocols. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T4#GNS112_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why would a doctor order a diagnostic thoracentesis?

options.A: To measure how much oxygen the lungs can hold total
options.B: To find out the exact cause of a pleural fluid buildup
options.C: To prevent the development of a future heart attack
options.D: To permanently cure chronic obstructive pulmonary disease

explanation: Great thinking! When we take a little sample of that fluid to the lab, we can figure out why it started gathering in the chest in the first place. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T17#GNS213_U2_T17_h1)

question: A patient with a head injury seems stable. Why must you keep monitoring them closely over the next few days?

options.A: Complications often develop hours or days after the primary injury
options.B: Hospital policies require discharges within 48 hours
options.C: Patients usually fake their symptoms to get more attention
options.D: Medications stop working completely after the first day

explanation: Brain swelling takes time to build up. A patient looking fine right now can take a sudden turn for the worse later, so constant watch is key! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T23#GNS222_U3_T23_h1)

question: A postpartum patient who delivered 24 hours ago asks why her blood sugar levels have suddenly dropped back to normal after needing insulin during pregnancy. What is the nurse's best response?

options.A: It is a sign that your kidneys are working too hard to filter extra sugar out of your blood.
options.B: The hormones from the placenta that caused insulin resistance were delivered with the baby.
options.C: This drop is only temporary and your blood sugar will spike again once your milk comes in.
options.D: Your pancreas has suddenly regenerated new cells to process all the sugar in your diet.

explanation: Once the placenta is expelled, the hormones causing gestational insulin resistance vanish, leading to an immediate drop in insulin requirements. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T7#GNS121_U7_T7_h6)

question: A client comes back complaining of mild spotting a month after getting an implant. How should you respond?

options.A: Tell her she has a serious pelvic infection
options.B: Take out the implant immediately and offer nothing else
options.C: Reassure her that this is a normal and common side effect
options.D: Tell her to stop drinking water for two days

explanation: Spot on! Pre-counseling helps clients stay calm. Reassuring them that spotting is normal builds great trust and keeps them comfortable. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T53#GNS214_U1_T53_h6)
